report.summary: Two separate root causes. The product bug is that GET /api/books and the /books page list every user's books, because list_books() never filters by owner_id; this breaks the API isolation test and makes a new user's empty-bookshelf page show another user's book. The test bug is that the UI page object clicks get_by_test_id("add-books") while the template's button is data-testid="add-book", which breaks both add-book UI tests. Fix the owner filter in app/main.py first, then correct the test id in tests/support/pages.py.

causes.title: Book listing returns every user's books
causes.explanation: list_books() runs an unfiltered SELECT over the books table and ignores its user_id argument. Both the JSON API (/api/books) and the server-rendered /books page call it, so any logged-in user sees every other user's books. This violates the per-user privacy the app is built around. The API test fails because the other user's listing contains the first user's book id. The login test fails because the freshly registered user's page lists a book created by another test's user, so the empty-state element never renders. The failure is deterministic for any shared database that already holds another user's book, so this is not flakiness.
evidence: app/main.py:147-150: def list_books(user_id: int) -> list[dict]: with db() as conn: rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()
tests/api/test_books_api.py:42: assert book["id"] not in other_ids  -> AssertionError: assert 2 not in [1, 2]
tests/ui/test_login_ui.py:14 (Aria snapshot): row "From API-d58f5c6c Robot Delete" is shown on the brand-new user's /books page, so get_by_test_id("empty-state") finds no element
Compare app/main.py:165-167, where get_own_book correctly filters with AND owner_id = ?, showing the intended pattern.
causes.suggested_fix: Change the query to "SELECT * FROM books WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY id" with (user_id,) and keep the rest of list_books as is. Add a regression test that two users each see only their own books through both the API and the UI.

causes.title: Page object uses wrong test id for the Add book button
causes.explanation: BooksPage.add() clicks get_by_test_id("add-books"), but the template's submit button is data-testid="add-book". The locator never matches, so Playwright times out after 5 s before any form input is submitted. Both UI tests that call add() fail at the same line for this reason. The application's button is correct, so the test helper is the thing to fix.
evidence: Failure output: Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for get_by_test_id("add-books")
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:13 and :42 both call books.add(...) and fail at pages.py:44
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/support/pages.py line 44, change get_by_test_id("add-books") to get_by_test_id("add-book"). Check whether the id was renamed in the template recently; if so, the template change is what should be reviewed. Then rerun both UI tests. The future-year test's later assertions (error text, retained title, no row created) look consistent with the app's behaviour in app/main.py:324-332, but they have not been exercised yet.
